scope: Unique three-place seed, four later three-output births, fourth taking three parents and exactly one of its three outputs spent. All other births take two or three parents and make two outputs. Rival arbitrary within the serial mixed law.
reader_input: Current named pair table up to a common arbitrary permutation, law, and proposed unordered triple. No distinguished birth site, output, or history.
conclusion: Once exactly one of the fourth junction’s outputs is spent, a live triple is possible and the same named triple can survive. At every finite size, distance five fixes both remaining loose outputs at a common holder and every other physical site of a live source. In the single-six case only four overlapping attachments of that site can vary. All 3,476 sources through width 29 have a unique physical completion. Whether an overlapping replacement can reverse a triple at larger widths is open.
primary_class: All-size structural reductions and subfamily permission theorems with exact finite formation closure, literal witnesses and a bounded full inverse. General one-spent permission prediction open.

predictions.claim: After the spend, a legal triple involving the fourth site or its child exists.
predictions.status: Proved; first legal at width 23, earliest surviving named triple at width 25.

predictions.claim: D≤5 preserves every three-parent verdict on every one-spent source against every reachable mixed rival.
predictions.status: Open. Complete through width 29 and proved at all sizes for stated subfamilies. D≤4 insufficient at width 23.

every_size: At any live source the two surviving outputs remain loose together in any D≤5 rival, all other ordinary junctions agree as physical supports, and each equally-loose bit keeps its holder. In the live two-six case all supports agree. In the single-six case at most 330 four-attachment sets remain, at most 126 with two shrinks; possible distinct sets must overlap.
Complete physical and menu recovery in the nonshrinking branch, sharply at D≤5, and in the single-six branch when the child is the only shrinking join even if its own outputs are later used.

When the spending child takes three parents and both its outputs are still loose, all triple permissions agree at D≤5. A binary spending child of an earlier ternary-third source with both child outputs loose also gives full physical recovery.

The closed row of the actually spent bit through the spending child’s arity recovers its parity equation at any depth. Across the entire mixed law, distinct rows exchangeable through D≤5 and of minimum row distance five have a common producing site.
The fixed point gives at most two shrinks on any positive O source, zero if the third birth took three parents. A live marked input persists along widths 33+4j.

interval.physical_inverse: Unique on every source, including empty menus, at D≤5 against every reachable rival.

residual: For a live source beyond width 29, can distinct overlapping four-subsets attached to the sole six-place site, with the identical recovered smaller physical supports and surviving pair, give the same full named table and different menus? Both sides must be reachable. An opposition in which only an unrestricted rival is live need not satisfy the live-source reduction. The larger four-addition and unrestricted source families remain open.
validation: V1 within-task symbolic proofs, independent proof audits and literal checks. Source-depth fixed point replayed under two hash seeds, named two-shrink example checked under permutation, connected cuts and independent parity-space minima agreed on all 465 entries of that width-31 example, arities 3–6 passed finite K1–K3. Separate referee pending.
assumptions: G1 gains a holder-recovery theorem. A97 remains under challenge. No new global default or change to goal wording.
